text:
Maya (PM): quick thread — we need to triage the post-launch backlog into LIFT vs SHELF vs EXPERIMENT for the next 2-week mini-iteration. goal: pick ~3 lifts that are low-risk/high-impact.
Jin (Eng): +1. can you share proposed criteria?
Maya (PM): criteria I was thinking: severity (P0/P1), paying-customer-affecting, time-to-fix (<=2d prefer), cross-team scope, and rollout risk. also prefer fixes that reduce unit cost.
Oliver (Infra): adding infra note: any KV-cache/oom work >2d tends to ripple. memory leak (BUG-1423) is prob 3d+ and touches runtime. recommend shelf unless Acme requests.
Priya (Design): UX polish on help flow is ~1d and users report frustration — high perceived value. I'd vote lift.
Sam (SRE): embeddings-drift alerts yesterday were noisy; that's regression-like. if it's a model mismatch we should lift to avoid churn.
Jin (Eng): quick estimates: BUG-1423 (mem leak) 3d, BUG-1501 (rate-limit bug) 1d, FEAT-298 (help UX polish) 6-8h, BUG-1600 (embed drift) 1-2d to triage + mitigation.
Maya (PM): propose initial picks for LIFT: BUG-1501 (rate-limit customer-facing), FEAT-298 (help UX polish), BUG-1600 (embed drift mitigation). Shelf: BUG-1423 mem leak (blocker but high effort), longtail perf tickets. Experiment: small perf caching trial for route-level batching.
Oliver (Infra): agree on list. for BUG-1501 I can do a focused patch + canary. need someone to own the canary run.
Sam (SRE): I can run the canary and monitor p99 and error spikes. recommend adding a short rollback playbook: revert to model-v2 and lower batch size.
Jin (Eng): tagging owners: BUG-1501 -> Jin, FEAT-298 -> Priya, BUG-1600 -> Jin+Sam. will add estimates to the ticket.
Maya (PM): ownership noted. I'll update the grooming board and add label `shelf/lift/experiment`. small ask: prioritize any customer SLA hits (Acme).
Priya (Design): quick mock for FEAT-298 done, posting screenshot in the ticket. tiny accessibility tweak included.
Jin (Eng): quick command I ran to find related errors:
```
rg "null pointer" -n logs/2025-*-*.log | head -n 50
```
Jin (Eng): preliminary root cause near header parsing, should be isolateable.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: `canary/acme-ratefix` at 1765547000 (UTC).
Maya (PM): nice. follow-ups: 1) grooming board updated, 2) owners assigned, 3) canary runway defined. can we sync in 30m to lock sprint?
Oliver (Infra): I'll free up 1/2 day to support canary and rollback testing.
Sam (SRE): I'll prepare dashboard and alert thresholds.
Maya (PM): ok locking decisions for now — lifts = BUG-1501, FEAT-298, BUG-1600. shelf mem leak for next major. experiment = route-level cache trial (opt-in). syncing in 30m. :thumbsup:
